title: An-Naba' 78:1-8 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: An-Naba' and Al-Qadr as a model
source: Written for quran/y7 lesson 37 (Pupil PDF worksheet: An-Naba' 78:1-8 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 37. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: عَمَّ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ (١) عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ (٢) ٱلَّذِى هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ (٣) كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ (٤) ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ (٥)
أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلْأَرْضَ مِهَٰدًۭا (٦) وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًۭا (٧) وَخَلَقْنَٰكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًۭا (٨)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: About what are they asking one another?
That over which they are in disagreement.
No! They are going to know.
Then, no! They are going to know.
Have We not made the earth a resting place?
And We created you in pairs

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Madd muttasil, then 'aarid at the stop

questions.q: Chunk and link An-Naba' 78:1-8 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 78:1-8 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 78:1-8 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Explain in one sentence how mountains are 'stakes' (78:7).
questions.a: Like tent pegs, they are fixed deep and give stability to the earth's surface.

questions.q: Why does 78:4 to 5 repeat 'No! They are going to know'?
questions.a: Repetition gives emphasis and warning: the truth will certainly become clear.

questions.q: Which signs of creation are named in 78:6 to 8?
options: The earth as a resting place, the mountains as stakes, people in pairs
The sun, the moon and the stars
questions.a: A) The earth as a resting place, the mountains as stakes, people in pairs. 78:6 to 8.

questions.q: Think again: People argue about many 'big questions'. What is 'the great news' (an-naba' al-'azim) that An-Naba' begins with?
questions.a: The news of the Resurrection and the Day of Judgement, which people disputed; Allah says they will come to know (78:4 to 5).
